content: The Birmingham Institute of Art and Design (BIAD) is recognized as the largest university-level art and design teaching and research institution in the United Kingdom outside of London. It operates as a part of Birmingham City University, which was previously known as Birmingham Polytechnic and later the University of Central England in Birmingham. The primary campus and library of BIAD are situated at Gosta Green, located just north of Birmingham city centre. This location is approximately three-quarters of a mile from both Birmingham New Street railway station and the Custard Factory quarter. In addition to the main campus, BIAD operates smaller specialized centres. The Bournville centre, located in the southern suburbs of the city, offers foundation-level awards and evening classes. The Margaret Street centre, situated in the city centre near Birmingham Central Library and Birmingham Museum & Art Gallery, focuses on Fine Art. The Vittoria Street centre, located in the Jewellery Quarter of the city, specializes in Jewellery design. Furthermore, the International Project Space at Bournville serves as a venue for hosting international art exhibitions and artist residencies. The Gosta Green campus is also home to the User-lab, a research and design laboratory that emphasizes user-centred design methodologies. The quality of BIAD’s programs has been recognized in various evaluations. For instance, the Sunday Times University Guide in 2004 rated its Art and Design programs as excellent with a score of 5. Additionally, Birmingham City University has highlighted that BIAD received a Quality Assurance score of 22 out of 24 for Art and Design from the Quality Assurance Agency (QAA). The origins of BIAD can be traced back to 1843, with its development reaching a significant milestone in the 1890s when it became the Birmingham Municipal School of Art at Margaret Street under the leadership of Edward R. Taylor. The institute’s archives house an extensive collection of records documenting the history of art and design in Birmingham. In addition, 20 other related collections have been deposited within these archives. Notable alumni of BIAD include Patrick le Quément, who served as the Chief of Design at Renault, and Vivien Hoffpauir, the founder and lead designer of Vivcore.
